the monoclonal antibodies used in this investigation can be divided into three major groups: (1) those that react with both haemopoietics and neural crest cells, (2) those that are reactive with neural crest but not haemopoietically derived cells, and (3) those that are specific for haemopoieticity but not for neural crest.
some haemopoietically defined monoclonals can be shown to react with neural crest derived tissues and some neural crest defined monoclonals with haemopoetic cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

monoclonal antibodies that have been raised to detect haemopoietically derived cells should be tested against a variety of cell types to determine their true specificity and to avoid the potential for erroneous conclusions being drawn.
the use of monoclonal antibodies to study haemopoietically derived cell subsets must take into account the possibility that the reagents used may be cross-reacting with antigens on other cell types.
the use of monoclonal antibodies to define cell types should always be accompanied by a thorough analysis of the cross-reactivity to other cell types.
